title: Shaderous setup
description: A simulation setup for Shaderous: the domain, the physics, the mesh, the background gas and the parts that make the initial conditions (docs/setups.md). Generated from the option table by `npm run gen`.

name.title: Name
name.description: What the setup is called in the preset list and in its file

blurb.title: Description
blurb.description: A sentence or two shown under the preset menu

ndim.title: Dimensions
ndim.description: Two or three dimensions. A 2D run is one layer of cells in x and y

n.title: Resolution
n.description: Cells across the box; on an adaptive mesh, at its finest level

amr.title: Refinement
amr.description: Adaptive mesh: levels of refinement below the coarsest grid. 0 puts every cell at the full resolution

box.title: Box size
box.description: Side of the box, in code units: the domain is a cube of this side centered on the origin

supports2d.title: Makes sense in 2D
supports2d.description: The setup can also run on a 2D (x, y) grid. Without it the setup is three-dimensional only

symmetric.title: Symmetric under
symmetric.description: The mirrors (planes through the origin, named by the axis normal to each) the setup is symmetric under: a run may then compute only the part above them

symmetricField.title: Field symmetric too
symmetricField.description: The magnetic field is symmetric under those mirrors as well (a vector potential odd in its normal component and even in the others)

mirror.title: Mirror symmetry
mirror.description: Compute only the part of a symmetric setup above its planes of symmetry: each mirrored axis runs from 0 to the box side, its lower face a plane of symmetry, and the totals are those of the whole. An octant in 3D (or a quadrant in 2D) gives twice the resolution for the same cells

geometry.title: Geometry
geometry.description: Cartesian, or a 2D body of revolution about the y axis, in (R, z): x is then R from the axis (the lower x face) to the box side, and cells are rings; or in (r, theta): x is then r from the inner radius to the box side, y theta from pole to pole

rMin.title: Inner radius
rMin.description: A spherical (r, theta) run: the radius of its inner face (above zero); the box side is then its outer radius

logR.title: Logarithmic in r
logR.description: A spherical (r, theta) run: cells spaced evenly in ln r, so that they stay about as long as they are wide, rather than evenly in r

bc.title: Faces of the box
bc.description: What the gas meets at each face of the box. Periodic faces come in pairs

xlo.title: Wall velocity, lower x face
xlo.description: Where the lower x face is a moving wall: its velocity along itself (the part normal to it is ignored)

xhi.title: Wall velocity, upper x face
xhi.description: Where the upper x face is a moving wall: its velocity along itself (the part normal to it is ignored)

ylo.title: Wall velocity, lower y face
ylo.description: Where the lower y face is a moving wall: its velocity along itself (the part normal to it is ignored)

yhi.title: Wall velocity, upper y face
yhi.description: Where the upper y face is a moving wall: its velocity along itself (the part normal to it is ignored)

zlo.title: Wall velocity, lower z face
zlo.description: Where the lower z face is a moving wall: its velocity along itself (the part normal to it is ignored)

zhi.title: Wall velocity, upper z face
zhi.description: Where the upper z face is a moving wall: its velocity along itself (the part normal to it is ignored)

name.title: Name
name.description: A name for the unit system

value.title: Length
value.description: This many of the unit beside it are one code unit of length

value.title: Mass
value.description: This many of the unit beside it are one code unit of mass

value.title: Density
value.description: This many of the unit beside it are one code unit of density

value.title: Velocity
value.description: This many of the unit beside it are one code unit of velocity

units.title: Physical units
units.description: What one code unit is, for a setup that stands for something real: a length and a mass (the time unit then makes G = 1), or a length, a density and a velocity. Without them the setup is scale free and shown in code units

eos.title: Equation of state
eos.description: How pressure follows from density and internal energy. Changing it carries each cell’s pressure over, and the run continues

gravity.title: Gravity
gravity.description: Off, a uniform field, or the self-gravity of the gas. Point masses pull either way

G.title: G
G.description: Gravitational constant in code units, or the strength of the uniform field. A setup with physical units may leave it to them

gext.title: Uniform acceleration
gext.description: A uniform acceleration on the gas, besides the Constant field

cooling.title: Cooling function
cooling.description: Optically thin radiative cooling (and heating) of the gas

viscosity.title: Viscosity ν
viscosity.description: Kinematic viscosity: the stress is ρ ν times the shear. Obstacles hold the gas at their walls. 0 is off

conductivity.title: Conductivity κ
conductivity.description: Thermal conduction: the heat flux is -κ ρ grad T, so the temperature of an ideal gas diffuses at (γ - 1) κ. 0 is off

resistivity.title: Resistivity η
resistivity.description: With a magnetic field: magnetic diffusivity, so the field diffuses as η ∇²B (the electric field gains η curl B) and the current it dissipates, η J², heats the gas. 0 is off (ideal MHD, with only the scheme’s own diffusion)

accel.title: Driving acceleration
accel.description: Turbulence driving: the root-mean-square acceleration of a random force that stirs the gas at large scales (a band of wavelengths, correlated over a time τ). The gas reaches speeds of about (accel × box / band)^½ where it balances the dissipation. 0 is off

tau.title: Driving correlation time τ
tau.description: How long the random force keeps its pattern (its Ornstein-Uhlenbeck correlation time)

kMin.title: Driving band, longest
kMin.description: The longest wavelengths driven, as wavelengths per box side

kMax.title: Driving band, shortest
kMax.description: The shortest wavelengths driven, as wavelengths per box side (at most 64 wavevectors are kept, the longest first)

zeta.title: Solenoidal share ζ
zeta.description: What the force stirs: 1 swirls only (solenoidal, no compression), 0 compresses only, 0.5 the natural mix

seed.title: Driving seed
seed.description: Which random force: each seed gives another, and the same seed the same run

riemann.title: Riemann solver
riemann.description: How the flux between neighboring cells is worked out. HLLC resolves contact waves; its low-Mach version cuts dissipation in slow flow; HLL is the most diffusive and the most robust

limiter.title: Limiter
limiter.description: How steeply the reconstruction may vary within a cell: Koren is sharpest, Minmod most diffusive and most robust

cfl.title: CFL number
cfl.description: Timestep as a fraction of the time a signal takes to cross a cell. Smaller is more stable and slower

rho.title: Density floor
rho.description: No cell is thinner than this

p.title: Pressure floor
p.description: No cell has less pressure than this

rho.title: Tenuous below density
rho.description: Gas thinner than this has its heat and speed capped (the next two fields), so a few hot or fast cells of ambient gas cannot set the timestep for the whole grid. Not conservative, but such gas carries next to no mass. 0 is off

u.title: Max specific energy
u.description: Largest internal energy per unit mass tenuous gas may have. 0 is no cap

v.title: Max speed
v.description: Largest speed tenuous gas may have. 0 is no cap

va.title: Max Alfvén speed
va.description: With a magnetic field: largest Alfvén speed |B| / √ρ anywhere. Where the field is stronger than that for the gas it threads, mass is added at rest until it is not. Not conservative. 0 is no cap

frame.title: Frame
frame.description: An inertial frame, or one that accelerates with the gas’s center of mass or the point masses’, so that what the run follows stays in the box

omega.title: Rotating frame Ω
omega.description: Angular velocity of a frame turning about an axis through the box center: the gas feels the Coriolis force (and the centrifugal force, below). Velocities are those in the turning frame. In 2D only the z part turns the plane. Zero: an inertial frame

centrifugal.title: Centrifugal force
centrifugal.description: With a rotating frame: the centrifugal force as well as the Coriolis force. Off, the Coriolis force alone (an f-plane, as in a shearing box)

omegaM.title: Matter density Ω_m
omegaM.description: Matter density today, in units of the critical density

omegaL.title: Cosmological constant Ω_Λ
omegaL.description: Its density today, in units of the critical density (the curvature makes up the rest)

zEnd.title: Ending redshift
zEnd.description: Redshift the run stops at (it sets the end time)

h.title: Hubble constant h
h.description: H0 in units of 100 km/s/Mpc, for the physical units a box size gives

boxMpc.title: Box size (Mpc/h)
boxMpc.description: The box’s comoving side in Mpc/h. With it the run has physical units, and the readouts show proper densities, pressures and lengths at the current scale factor. Left out, the run is scale free

cosmology.title: Comoving coordinates
cosmology.description: An expanding universe: positions comoving, densities comoving (mean 1), velocities peculiar, times in 1/H0 from the starting redshift. G follows from the matter density. A periodic box of gas, with or without self-gravity

q.title: Shear q
q.description: -d ln Ω / d ln R: 1.5 for a Keplerian disk, 1 for a flat rotation curve

stratified.title: Stratified
stratified.description: The vertical tidal pull, -Ω² z, toward the midplane

shear.title: Shearing box
shear.description: The local model of a disk: a frame turning at Ω about z with the tidal pull of the shear, x radial, y along the orbit. Its x faces are periodic with the shift of the background flow v_y = -q Ω x, which the initial state should hold. Hydrodynamics on a uniform grid, periodic in y (and z unless stratified)

jeansFloor.title: Jeans floor
jeansFloor.description: Pressure floor that keeps the Jeans length resolved (Truelove)

jeansCells.title: Cells per Jeans length
jeansCells.description: The Jeans floor raises the pressure so the Jeans length spans at least this many cells

vcycles.title: V-cycles
vcycles.description: Multigrid V-cycles per step for self-gravity. More converge the potential further, at more cost. On the adaptive mesh this is the most per step

gravEnergyFlux.title: Conserve energy
gravEnergyFlux.description: Flux-form gravitational work: conserves total energy

composition.title: Composition
composition.description: What the gas is made of, which sets the kelvin scale and the physical constants of the equation of state: solar (fully ionized), solarNeutral, hydrogen or carbonOxygen

species.title: Species
species.description: Species whose mass fractions the gas carries, by name (he4, c12, ...), separated by commas; or aprox13 for the burning network’s thirteen. None by default

speciesGamma.title: Gamma by species
speciesGamma.description: Adiabatic index of each species the gas carries, by name, where the species set the equation of state (a mixture of ideal gases): a species not listed takes the gas’s gamma

burn.title: Burning
burn.description: Burning of the gas, wherever it is hot and dense enough: nuclear, by the trained network of the 13-isotope alpha chain, or a single fuel to ash reaction at an Arrhenius rate

rho.title: Density
rho.description: The tools’ density scale is at least this

v.title: Speed
v.description: The tools’ speed scale is at least this

toolScale.title: Scale of the editing tools
toolScale.description: Least density and speed the editing tools (paint, push) measure their amounts against. They take the densest and fastest gas of the run, which leaves them nothing to go by in a box that holds next to nothing

refineHi.title: Refine above
refineHi.description: Adaptive mesh: a block is split where the normalized second derivative of density or pressure exceeds this anywhere in it. The indicator is near 1 at a shock or contact and small where the gas varies smoothly. Lower refines more

refineLo.title: Merge below
refineLo.description: Adaptive mesh: four sibling blocks are merged where the indicator is below this in all of them. Kept below the refinement threshold

refineMasses.title: Refine around point masses
refineMasses.description: Adaptive mesh: keep the gas around every point mass at the finest level, so that softening and sinks can be as small as the finest cells allow

refineDense.title: Always refine above density
refineDense.description: Adaptive mesh: gas denser than this is always at the finest level, as the smooth interior of a star must be. 0 is off

refineRho.title: Refine above density
refineRho.description: Adaptive mesh: gas thinner than this does not ask for refinement, so ripples in the ambient gas far from a star leave its blocks coarse. 0 is off

timeBins.title: Local timesteps
timeBins.description: Adaptive mesh: blocks of slow gas take longer steps than the fastest block, where that saves work

jeansRefine.title: Refine the Jeans length
jeansRefine.description: With self-gravity, refine where the Jeans length is under this many cells. 0 is off

rho.title: Ambient density
rho.description: Density of the gas that fills the box where no part puts anything else. With stars, the gas around them

p.title: Ambient pressure
p.description: Pressure of that gas. With stars and left empty, the pressure of the stars’ outermost layer

s.title: Ambient dye
s.description: Passive scalar of that gas: a dye carried with it

X.title: Ambient composition
X.description: Mass fractions of that gas, by species name

cut.title: Stars end at density
cut.description: With stars: a cell thinner than this is ambient gas, not star. Left empty, a polytrope ends where the ambient gas would be as hot as its center

tEnd.title: End time
tEnd.description: The run pauses when it reaches this time. Empty runs on without end

checkpointDt.title: Checkpoint every
checkpointDt.description: Time between checkpoints, when the page is asked to save them: the value the Time panel starts with

tDyn.title: Dynamical time
tDyn.description: The time over which the flow visibly changes (a star’s sqrt(R³ / G M), a binary’s period): a movie takes a frame every 600th of it by default

startPaused.title: Start paused
startPaused.description: The run waits, paused, for Run

field.title: Opening field
field.description: The quantity shown when the setup opens (the View panel’s Field, by its number)

log.title: Logarithmic colors
log.description: The color scale the setup opens with

mode.title: Opening view
mode.description: How the gas is drawn when the setup opens in 3D

axis.title: Slice normal
axis.description: The axis the opening slice is perpendicular to (0 x, 1 y, 2 z)

pitch.title: Camera elevation
pitch.description: Elevation of the volume view’s camera when the setup opens, in radians

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

gm.title: G M
gm.description: Its mass times G, in code units

pos.title: Position
pos.description: Where it starts, relative to the box center

vel.title: Velocity
vel.description: How it moves at the start

soft.title: Softening
soft.description: Plummer softening length of its gravity: at least two cells, and two cells if left empty. Changes take effect without a restart

sink.title: Sink radius
sink.description: Radius within which it takes gas in: the softening length if left empty, 0 for none. Changes take effect without a restart

sinkRate.title: Sink rate
sinkRate.description: Removal rate at the sink’s center, in units of sqrt(G M / radius³)

massless.title: Massless
massless.description: A particle without a mass of its own: it pulls on nothing and moves as the gas and the masses pull it

fixed.title: Held in place
fixed.description: Nothing moves it, whatever pulls on it or it takes in

onOrbit.title: Hold on its orbit
onOrbit.description: The other point masses move it; the gas does not: neither the gas’s pull nor what its sink takes changes its motion, and it does not grow. A binary with both masses held keeps the orbit it was given, as in most studies of circumbinary disks. What the sink takes is still counted. Changes take effect without a restart

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

of.title: Bodies
of.description: The two bodies it places: two point masses (binary), a star and a point mass (flyby), or two stars (collision)

type.title: Kind of orbit
type.description: Binary: two point masses about their center of mass, at pericenter. Flyby: a point mass on a parabola about a star that stays at the origin (a tidal disruption in the star’s frame). Collision: two stars on a parabola about their center of mass

q.title: Mass ratio
q.description: Mass of the second body over the first. It sets their masses: in a binary the total stays, in a flyby the star’s

separation.title: Separation
separation.description: Semi-major axis of the binary’s orbit

incl.title: Inclination (°)
incl.description: Tilt of the binary’s orbit about the line through pericenter, in degrees (3D): 180 is retrograde

beta.title: Impact parameter β
beta.description: Tidal radius over pericenter distance: above 1 the mass passes inside the star’s tidal radius

start.title: Starts at (tidal radii)
start.description: Separation at the start, in tidal radii (never inside 1.5 pericenters)

impact.title: Impact parameter
impact.description: Pericenter distance over the sum of the two radii: 0 is head-on, 1 just grazes

starts.title: Starts at (sums of radii)
starts.description: Separation at the start, in sums of the two radii (closer if they would not fit in the box)

debris.title: Debris energies
debris.description: Bin the star’s gas by its orbital energy about the mass, for the rate at which bound debris returns

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

type.title: Kind of star
type.description: A polytrope of index n, or a cold white dwarf held up by degenerate electrons

n.title: Polytropic index n
n.description: The star’s structure, p = K ρ^(1 + 1/n): the larger n, the more centrally concentrated. Stable against convection only if the gas’s adiabatic index is at least 1 + 1/n

radius.title: Radius
radius.description: A polytrope’s radius, in code units. A white dwarf’s follows from its mass

mass.title: Mass
mass.description: Its mass, in code units (solar masses for a white dwarf in its usual units)

rhoc.title: Central density
rhoc.description: Instead of the mass: a polytrope’s central density

pos.title: Position
pos.description: Where it starts, relative to the box center

vel.title: Velocity
vel.description: How it moves at the start

dye.title: Dye
dye.description: Passive scalar of its gas, which tells the stars apart: spread over (0, 1] by their order if left empty

X.title: Composition
X.description: Mass fractions of its gas, by species name (the ambient gas’s if left empty)

type.title: Shape
type.description: Dipole or random, by the plasma beta at the center; or Guillochon & McCourt’s, by β_M

beta.title: Plasma beta
beta.description: Gas pressure over magnetic pressure B² / 2 at the center (or β_M): the larger, the weaker the field

seed.title: Random seed
seed.description: Which random field: each seed gives another

field.title: Magnetic field inside
field.description: A field confined to the star: a dipole along z or a tangled Kolmogorov field, with plasma beta at the center; or the same as Guillochon & McCourt (2017) set them, by their β_M

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

about.title: Orbits
about.description: The point masses or stars it orbits: about several, their total mass. The disk is centered on their center of mass and moves with it. About a star, keep the inner radius outside 1.3 of the star’s radius: the star is settled within that

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: Thin: a surface density with a cavity and a Gaussian vertical profile, on circular orbits (the binary’s disk). Balanced: a midplane density in vertical balance with the softened potential, rotating as its pressure gradient asks (the magnetized disk); 3D only

radialFn.title: Radial profile (formula)
radialFn.description: A density profile of your own in radius, as a formula of r: the surface density (thin) or the midplane density (balanced). It replaces the density scale’s law, the slope and the tapers. Example: sigma0 * (r / rIn)^-1 * exp(-(r / rOut)^2) * step(r - rIn). Names: r, rIn, rOut, sigma0, cs, H (the scale height cs / Ω at r), pi, e. Functions: exp, log, ln, log10, sqrt, abs, sin, cos, tan, atan, sinh, cosh, tanh, step, pow, min, max, clamp; powers as x^y. Where it is not a positive number there is no disk. A file may give a table of points instead (radial)

verticalFn.title: Vertical profile (formula)
verticalFn.description: A density profile of your own in height, as a formula of z, the height above the midplane (the same on both sides), relative to the midplane: it replaces the Gaussian (thin) or the balance with the potential (balanced). Examples: exp(-z^2 / 2), 1 / cosh(z)^2, max(1 - z / 3, 0). Such a disk is in vertical balance only if the profile is, and settles as the run starts. 3D only. A file may give a table of points instead (vertical)

verticalIn.title: Heights in
verticalIn.description: The z of the vertical profile: in scale heights cs / Ω of each radius (the profile then flares with the disk), or in code lengths

rIn.title: Inner radius
rIn.description: Where the disk is tapered away toward the center (the cavity’s radius)

rOut.title: Outer radius
rOut.description: Where the disk is tapered away outward

sigma0.title: Density scale
sigma0.description: Thin: the surface density. Balanced: the midplane density at r = 1

slope.title: Density slope
slope.description: Balanced: the midplane density goes as r to this power (-3/2 is a flat surface density)

cs.title: Sound speed
cs.description: Sound speed of the disk’s gas: its scale height is cs / Ω

floor.title: Gas outside the disk
floor.description: Thin: a fraction of the density scale. Balanced: the density of the ambient gas

from.title: Damping from r
from.description: Radius from the box center where the damping zone starts

rate.title: Damping rate
rate.description: How many times per local orbital period the gas at the box edge is relaxed toward its initial state. 0 is off

damp.title: Damping zone
damp.description: Beyond a radius the gas is relaxed toward the disk as it started, more strongly toward the box’s edge, so the outer disk is a reservoir and the boundaries see only it

beta.title: Plasma beta at the midplane
beta.description: Gas pressure over magnetic pressure where two loops meet: the larger, the weaker the field

span.title: Span of a loop
span.description: Each loop spans this factor in radius

count.title: Loops
count.description: How many loops, outward from the inner radius

loops.title: Field loops
loops.description: Poloidal loops of magnetic field inside the disk, with no net flux: the seed of the magnetorotational instability (balanced profile)

stresses.title: Disk diagnostics
stresses.description: Report the disk’s stresses and MRI quality factors about the first point mass

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

type.title: Shape
type.description: A sphere (a cylinder in 2D), a box, or the half of space on one side of a plane

radiusCells.title: Radius in cells
radiusCells.description: Instead of the radius: this many finest cells, whatever the resolution (a point explosion)

normal.title: Normal
normal.description: The plane’s normal: the shape is the side the normal points away from

at.title: Plane at
at.description: Distance of the plane from the box center, along its normal

rotate.title: Rotation
rotate.description: Degrees the box is turned about its center: about x, then y, then z. In 2D only the turn about z counts

energy.title: Total energy
energy.description: Instead of a pressure: this much energy in all, spread evenly over the sphere’s cells (a point explosion; per unit length in 2D)

X.title: Composition
X.description: Mass fractions inside the shape, by species name

supersample.title: Smooth edge (samples)
supersample.description: A sphere’s edge cells take the share of their volume inside it, from this many samples a side. Empty: a sharp edge

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

type.title: Shape
type.description: A sphere (a cylinder in 2D), a box, or the half of space on one side of a plane

radiusCells.title: Radius in cells
radiusCells.description: Instead of the radius: this many finest cells, whatever the resolution (a point explosion)

normal.title: Normal
normal.description: The plane’s normal: the shape is the side the normal points away from

at.title: Plane at
at.description: Distance of the plane from the box center, along its normal

rotate.title: Rotation
rotate.description: Degrees the box is turned about its center: about x, then y, then z. In 2D only the turn about z counts

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

type.title: Shape
type.description: A sphere (a cylinder in 2D), a box, or the half of space on one side of a plane

radiusCells.title: Radius in cells
radiusCells.description: Instead of the radius: this many finest cells, whatever the resolution (a point explosion)

normal.title: Normal
normal.description: The plane’s normal: the shape is the side the normal points away from

at.title: Plane at
at.description: Distance of the plane from the box center, along its normal

rotate.title: Rotation
rotate.description: Degrees the box is turned about its center: about x, then y, then z. In 2D only the turn about z counts

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

up.title: Strength, upward
up.description: Instead of a vector: a strength along the axis drawn upward (y in 2D, z in 3D)

oneOf.title: Flow: Advected Gaussian blob

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: A Gaussian density blob at the center, carried by a uniform flow at a uniform pressure. The passive scalar follows the blob. On a periodic box it tests conservation.

oneOf.title: Flow: Alfven-wave collision

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: Two plane Alfven waves travelling in opposite directions along a guide field B0 (along z), in uniform gas of density 1: one varies along x and is polarized along y, the other varies along y and is polarized along x (Howes & Nielson 2013). Needs a 3D periodic box.

oneOf.title: Flow: Elsasser packets

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: Two Alfven-wave packets on a guide field B0 (along z), each with a Gaussian profile along the field: a z+ packet above the center heading down and a z- packet below it heading up, in uniform gas of density 1 (Verniero et al. 2018). They meet at the center at t = box / (4 B0). Needs a 3D periodic box.

oneOf.title: Flow: Carbon–oxygen fuel with an ignition layer

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: Carbon and oxygen at rest at one density, with a hot layer at the low-x edge of the box that sets it alight. Needs physical units, an equation of state with a temperature (Helmholtz) and the species of the aprox13 network.

oneOf.title: Flow: ZND detonation

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: The steady (ZND) detonation of the single-step Arrhenius model, moving toward +x into fuel of density 1 and pressure 1 (for gamma = 1.2; heat release 50), with its burning. Lengths are half-reaction lengths. Needs the species fuel and ash.

oneOf.title: Flow: Evrard sphere

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: A cold gas sphere whose density falls as 1/r, rho = M / (2 pi R^2 r), in thin gas at the same specific internal energy (for gamma = 5/3). With G = M = R = 1 it collapses in about a unit of time.

oneOf.title: Flow: Helium shell with a hot spot

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: Turns the outermost mass of the first star into helium over a carbon-oxygen core and heats a spot at the base of that shell, on the +z axis. Needs the 13 species of the burning network, the tabulated equation of state and physical units.

oneOf.title: Flow: Turbulent velocity field

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: Uniform gas in a unit periodic box, stirred by a few long-wavelength velocity modes with random directions and phases. With the preset’s isothermal gas (sound speed 0.1) the default speed is Mach 5.

oneOf.title: Flow: Jeans-unstable wave

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: A small adiabatic density wave along x about density 1 and sound speed 1. With one wavelength across a unit box and G = 2 pi it grows at the rate 2 pi; a shorter wave grows more slowly, or oscillates as sound once k^2 passes 4 pi G.

oneOf.title: Flow: Kelvin-Helmholtz shear layer

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: A dense slab across the middle of the box (in y), sliding through lighter gas at one pressure, with one seeded mode at its two edges. With helium, the slab is helium in hydrogen (species he4 and h1, which then set the equation of state), denser by the ratio of their mean molecular weights.

oneOf.title: Flow: Orszag-Tang vortex

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: The Orszag-Tang vortex on a periodic unit box (for gamma = 5/3): uniform gas of density 25 / 36 pi and pressure 5 / 12 pi (sound speed 1) with a velocity vortex and a field of twice its wavenumber in x.

oneOf.title: Flow: Rotor

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: A dense disk spinning rigidly in gas of density 1 at rest, at one pressure, with a ring around it where density and speed taper (Balsara & Spicer 1999). The field is a part of its own.

oneOf.title: Flow: Brio-Wu shock tube

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: The MHD shock tube of Brio & Wu (1988) along x (for gamma = 2): gas at rest in two states either side of a membrane at the center, a field B_x throughout and B_y reversing across the membrane.

oneOf.title: Flow: Field loop advection

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: A weak loop of magnetic field, A_z = A0 (R - r) inside radius R, in gas of density 1 and pressure 1 carried by a uniform flow: at (2, 1) on a periodic unit box it is back where it started at t = 1 (Gardiner & Stone 2005).

oneOf.title: Flow: Circularly polarized Alfven wave

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: A circularly polarized Alfven wave along the diagonal of the x-y plane of a periodic unit box: density 1, a field of 1 along the wave, and a perpendicular field and velocity that turn about it (Toth 2000). It returns to its start after each period, 1 / sqrt(2).

oneOf.title: Flow: Weak in-plane field

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: A weak tangled magnetic field in the x-y plane (random modes of the periodic box, from a vector potential A_z), for the flow to stretch and wind up. It adds to the other parts’ fields and leaves the gas as they paint it.

oneOf.title: Flow: Rayleigh-Taylor layers

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: Heavy gas over light gas in a unit box, in hydrostatic balance with the uniform downward acceleration of the setup (Gravity: Uniform acceleration), with one seeded mode that vanishes at the walls. Up is y in 2D and z in 3D.

oneOf.title: Flow: Harris current sheet

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: A current sheet along y = 0: B_x = B0 tanh(y / a), with the gas pressure higher in the sheet so that p + B² / 2 is uniform, density 1, an optional uniform guide field B_z, and a perturbation A_z = psi B0 L cos(k x) cos(pi y / L) that seeds the tearing mode (Harris 1962; Furth, Killeen & Rosenbluth 1963). Periodic along x, walls along y.

oneOf.title: Flow: Island coalescence

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: A chain of magnetic islands along y = 0, the Fadeev equilibrium A_z = -lambda B0 ln(cosh(y / lambda) + eps cos(x / lambda)), with the gas pressure p = p_out + B0² (1 - eps²) / (2 (cosh(y / lambda) + eps cos(x / lambda))²) that holds it, density 1, and a flow along x that pushes pairs of islands together (Fadeev et al. 1965; Finn & Kaw 1977). Periodic along x, walls along y.

oneOf.title: Flow: Stressed X-point

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: An X-type magnetic null at the center, A_z = (B0 / 2L) (y² - alpha² x²) with L the box side, so B = (B0 / L) (y, alpha² x), in gas of density 1 and uniform pressure. With alpha above 1 it carries a current its own force cannot hold, and collapses into a current sheet. Needs walls that hold the field lines crossing them: line-tied on all four sides.

oneOf.title: Flow: Shearing wave

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: The background flow of a shearing sheet, v_y = -q Omega x, with a small density wave cos(kx x + ky y) on it (kx and ky in wavelengths across the box). A leading wave (kx < 0) is swung to trailing by the shear and amplified on the way. Needs physics.shear.

oneOf.title: Flow: Shearing box

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: The background flow of a shearing box, v_y = -q Omega x, in gas of uniform density 1 and pressure, with small random velocities on it (a fraction of the sound speed) to seed instabilities such as the magnetorotational. Needs physics.shear.

oneOf.title: Flow: Shock hitting a helium bubble

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: A planar shock in air (density 1, pressure 1, gamma 1.4) running toward +x into a bubble of helium at the same pressure and temperature, after Haas & Sturtevant (1987). Needs the species he4 and air, in that order, each with its own gamma.

oneOf.title: Flow: Gas in unstable thermal balance

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: Uniform gas at the temperature where interstellar cooling balances heating on the unstable branch, with small random density perturbations at one pressure. Density in atoms per cm^3, temperature in units of 1000 K: needs the interstellar cooling, in those units.

oneOf.title: Flow: Zel’dovich pancake

id.description: A name other parts refer to it by (an orbit’s `of`, a disk’s `about`)

oneOf.description: One plane wave along x on its growing mode in an Einstein-de Sitter universe (physics.cosmology with Omega_m = 1): the gas converges into a sheet, a caustic, at the given redshift, and then shocks. Cold gas: its specific internal energy at the start is given.
